plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated interval session for developing threshold power.
Features a longer, controlled endurance run (107 minutes) to build sustained aerobic capacity.
Incorporates strength and mobility work, crucial for injury prevention and efficient running.
plan_b_advantages: Focuses on hill repeats, which are beneficial for trail running strength and technique.
Includes active recovery runs, which can be helpful for managing fatigue and promoting recovery.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a more targeted approach to improving aerobic power with a dedicated interval session, alongside a longer, controlled endurance run. Plan B, while including hill work, relies heavily on easy runs and recovery, which, while important, doesn't directly address the need for increased speed and power. Plan A’s structured sessions and inclusion of strength work are more aligned with a goal of improving performance, whereas Plan B feels more geared towards maintenance and recovery.
